ram_2392.name: Ram
ram_2392.who: A man of Judah, the firstborn son of Jerahmeel, named in Chronicles' genealogy of Judah.
key: Ram is named as the firstborn of Jerahmeel, who was Hezron's firstborn son (1 Chronicles 2).
His sons were Maaz, Jamin, and Eker (1 Chronicles 2).

rechab_2402.name: Rechab
rechab_2402.who: A Benjaminite raiding captain from Beeroth who, with his brother Baanah, murdered Saul's son Ish-bosheth.
key: Rechab and his brother Baanah, sons of Rimmon of Beeroth, led raiding bands for Ish-bosheth (2 Samuel 4).
They entered Ish-bosheth's house at midday, killed him on his bed, and beheaded him (2 Samuel 4).
They brought the head to David at Hebron, expecting a reward (2 Samuel 4).
David had them executed for killing a righteous man and hung their bodies beside the pool at Hebron (2 Samuel 4).

rechab_2404.name: Rechab
rechab_2404.who: The father of Malchijah, the district ruler who repaired Jerusalem's Dung Gate in Nehemiah's day.
key: His son Malchijah ruled the district of Beth-haccherem (Nehemiah 3).
Malchijah rebuilt the Dung Gate, setting its doors, bolts, and bars (Nehemiah 3).

rehob_2410.name: Rehob
rehob_2410.who: The father of Hadadezer, the king of Zobah in Syria whom David defeated.
key: David defeated Rehob's son Hadadezer, king of Zobah, in battle (2 Samuel 8).
David took Hadadezer's gold shields and much bronze to Jerusalem (2 Samuel 8).

rehum_2416.name: Rehum
rehum_2416.who: One of the chiefs of the people who set their seal on the covenant in Nehemiah's day.
key: After confessing their sins, the returned exiles made a firm written covenant (Nehemiah 9).
Rehum was among the chiefs of the people who sealed it (Nehemiah 10).
The signers pledged to keep God's law, honor the Sabbath, and support the temple (Nehemiah 10).

reumah_2433.name: Reumah
reumah_2433.who: The concubine of Nahor, Abraham's brother, and mother of four of his sons.
key: Abraham heard news of his brother Nahor's family, including his concubine Reumah (Genesis 22).
She bore Nahor four sons: Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah (Genesis 22).

rezon_2437.name: Rezon
rezon_2437.who: A Syrian leader who seized Damascus and became an adversary of Israel throughout Solomon's reign.
key: Rezon son of Eliada fled from his master Hadadezer, king of Zobah (1 Kings 11).
After David defeated Zobah, he gathered men around him and led a raiding band (1 Kings 11).
His band went to Damascus, and he reigned there over Syria (1 Kings 11).
God raised him up as an adversary, and he troubled Israel all the days of Solomon (1 Kings 11).

rhoda_2439.name: Rhoda
rhoda_2439.who: A servant girl in the Jerusalem house of Mary, mother of John Mark, who answered Peter's knock.
key: After an angel freed Peter from prison, Rhoda came to answer his knock at the gate (Acts 12).
Recognizing Peter's voice, in her joy she ran in to tell the others without opening the gate (Acts 12).
The praying believers said she was out of her mind, but Peter kept knocking until they let him in (Acts 12).

riphath_2443.name: Riphath
riphath_2443.who: A grandson of Japheth through Gomer, named in the table of nations after the flood.
key: Riphath is listed as a son of Gomer, son of Japheth, in the table of nations (Genesis 10).
Chronicles repeats him among Gomer's sons, with Ashkenaz and Togarmah (1 Chronicles 1).

rizpah_2444.name: Rizpah
rizpah_2444.who: A concubine of King Saul who kept watch over the bodies of her executed sons.
key: Rizpah daughter of Aiah was a concubine of King Saul (2 Samuel 3).
Ish-bosheth accused Abner of sleeping with her, and the angry Abner turned to support David (2 Samuel 3).
Her sons Armoni and Mephibosheth were among seven of Saul's descendants given to the Gibeonites and killed (2 Samuel 21).
She spread sackcloth on a rock and guarded their bodies from birds and beasts until the rains came (2 Samuel 21).
Hearing of it, David buried the bones of Saul and Jonathan along with the seven (2 Samuel 21).

rufus_2448.name: Rufus
rufus_2448.who: A son of Simon of Cyrene, the man compelled to carry Jesus' cross.
key: Mark names Rufus and his brother Alexander as sons of Simon of Cyrene (Mark 15).
Their father Simon was forced by the soldiers to carry Jesus' cross (Mark 15).

sabtah_2451.name: Sabtah
sabtah_2451.who: A son of Cush and grandson of Ham, named in the table of nations after the flood.
key: Sabtah is listed as a son of Cush, son of Ham, in the table of nations (Genesis 10).
Chronicles repeats him among the sons of Cush (1 Chronicles 1).

sapphira_2472.name: Sapphira
sapphira_2472.who: Wife of Ananias in the early Jerusalem church; both died after lying about money from land they sold.
key: With her husband Ananias she sold property and knowingly kept back part of the price (Acts 5).
About three hours after Ananias died, Peter asked her the sale price, and she lied (Acts 5).
Peter said they had agreed to test the Spirit of the Lord, and she fell down dead (Acts 5).
Young men buried her beside her husband, and great fear came on the whole church (Acts 5).

sceva_2480.name: Sceva
sceva_2480.who: A Jewish chief priest whose seven sons tried to cast out an evil spirit in Jesus' name at Ephesus.
key: Sceva was a Jewish chief priest whose seven sons were traveling exorcists in Ephesus (Acts 19).
His sons tried to cast out an evil spirit in the name of the Jesus whom Paul preached (Acts 19).
The possessed man overpowered them, and they fled from the house naked and wounded (Acts 19).
The event became known throughout Ephesus, and the name of the Lord Jesus was honored (Acts 19).

seba_2481.name: Seba
seba_2481.who: A son of Cush and grandson of Ham, named in the table of nations after the flood.
key: Seba is listed first among the sons of Cush, son of Ham, in the table of nations (Genesis 10).
Chronicles repeats him among the sons of Cush (1 Chronicles 1).

segub_2484.name: Segub
segub_2484.who: A man of Judah, son of Hezron by the daughter of Machir, and father of Jair of Gilead.
key: At sixty, Hezron married the daughter of Machir, father of Gilead, and she bore Segub (1 Chronicles 2).
Segub fathered Jair, who held twenty-three cities in the land of Gilead (1 Chronicles 2).

seir_2485.name: Seir
seir_2485.who: Seir the Horite, ancestor of the people who lived in the land of Edom before Esau's descendants.
key: Seir the Horite's sons are listed as the inhabitants of the land before Esau's descendants (Genesis 36).
His sons Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan became Horite chiefs (Genesis 36).
Chronicles repeats the list of his sons (1 Chronicles 1).

serah_2492.name: Serah
serah_2492.who: A daughter of Asher and granddaughter of Jacob, one of the few women named in Israel's genealogies.
key: Serah, daughter of Asher, is listed among Jacob's family who went down to Egypt (Genesis 46).
She is named again in the census of Asher's clans on the plains of Moab (Numbers 26).
Chronicles lists her as the sister of Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah (1 Chronicles 7).

seraiah_2495.name: Seraiah
seraiah_2495.who: An army captain of Judah, son of Tanhumeth, who joined Governor Gedaliah at Mizpah after Jerusalem fell.
key: After Babylon destroyed Jerusalem, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth was among the captains still in the field (2 Kings 25).
He and other captains came to Gedaliah at Mizpah when Babylon appointed him governor (2 Kings 25).
Gedaliah assured them they could live safely in the land by serving the king of Babylon (Jeremiah 40).

seraiah_2496.name: Seraiah
seraiah_2496.who: A man of Judah, son of Kenaz and brother of Othniel, Israel's first judge.
key: Chronicles lists Othniel and Seraiah as the sons of Kenaz in Judah's genealogy (1 Chronicles 4).
Seraiah fathered Joab, the father of Ge-harashim, a settlement of craftsmen (1 Chronicles 4).

seraiah_2497.name: Seraiah
seraiah_2497.who: A man of the tribe of Simeon, son of Asiel, whose grandson Jehu was a clan chief.
key: Seraiah son of Asiel is named in Simeon's genealogy as grandfather of Jehu, a chief (1 Chronicles 4).
In Hezekiah's days these Simeonite chiefs took pastureland near Gedor and settled there (1 Chronicles 4).

seraiah_2498.name: Seraiah
seraiah_2498.who: A priest who returned from exile with Zerubbabel and whose name was carried on by a priestly family.
key: A Seraiah is named among the leaders who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2).
The name Seraiah heads the priests who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah's day (Nehemiah 10).
Seraiah is first among the priests who came up with Zerubbabel (Nehemiah 12).
In the days of the high priest Joiakim, Meraiah led the priestly house of Seraiah (Nehemiah 12).

seraiah_2499.name: Seraiah
seraiah_2499.who: An officer of King Jehoiakim, son of Azriel, sent to arrest Jeremiah and Baruch.
key: After burning Jeremiah's scroll, Jehoiakim ordered Seraiah son of Azriel and others to seize Baruch and Jeremiah (Jeremiah 36).
They could not find them, for the LORD had hidden them (Jeremiah 36).

seraiah_2500.name: Seraiah
seraiah_2500.who: A royal staff officer, brother of Baruch, who carried Jeremiah's prophecy against Babylon to that city.
key: Seraiah son of Neriah was quartermaster when he went with King Zedekiah to Babylon (Jeremiah 51).
Jeremiah gave him a book of the disasters coming on Babylon, to read aloud there (Jeremiah 51).
He was then to tie a stone to it and throw it into the Euphrates (Jeremiah 51).
The sinking book was a sign that Babylon would sink and rise no more (Jeremiah 51).

sergius_2502.name: Sergius Paulus
sergius_2502.who: The Roman proconsul of Cyprus who believed after hearing Barnabas and Saul preach.
key: Sergius Paulus, an intelligent man, was proconsul of Cyprus at Paphos (Acts 13).
He summoned Barnabas and Saul because he wanted to hear the word of God (Acts 13).
The magician Elymas opposed them, and Paul declared he would be blind for a time (Acts 13).
Seeing this, the proconsul believed, astonished at the teaching of the Lord (Acts 13).

shallum_2514.name: Shallum
shallum_2514.who: A king of Israel who seized the throne by assassination and reigned only one month.
key: Shallum son of Jabesh conspired against King Zechariah of Israel, killed him, and took the throne (2 Kings 15).
Zechariah's death fulfilled the LORD's word that Jehu's dynasty would last four generations (2 Kings 15).
Shallum reigned one month in Samaria, in the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah king of Judah (2 Kings 15).
Menahem son of Gadi came from Tirzah, killed Shallum, and reigned in his place (2 Kings 15).

shallun_2527.name: Shallun
shallun_2527.who: Ruler of the district of Mizpah who rebuilt Jerusalem's Fountain Gate in Nehemiah's day.
key: Shallun son of Col-hozeh ruled the district of Mizpah when Jerusalem's wall was rebuilt (Nehemiah 3).
He rebuilt the Fountain Gate, roofing it and setting its doors, bolts, and bars (Nehemiah 3).
He also built the wall of the Pool of Shelah by the king's garden (Nehemiah 3).

shamgar_2534.name: Shamgar
shamgar_2534.who: A deliverer of Israel after Ehud, who struck down six hundred Philistines with an oxgoad.
key: After Ehud, Shamgar son of Anath killed six hundred Philistines with an oxgoad (Judges 3).
By this he also saved Israel (Judges 3).
Deborah's song recalls that in his days the main roads were abandoned and travelers used byways (Judges 5).

shammah_2538.name: Shammah
shammah_2538.who: A grandson of Esau through Reuel, and a chief among the Edomites.
key: Shammah was a son of Reuel, Esau's son by Basemath (Genesis 36).
He became one of the chiefs of Edom descended from Reuel (Genesis 36).
Chronicles repeats him among Reuel's sons (1 Chronicles 1).

shammah_2539.name: Shammah
shammah_2539.who: Son of Agee the Hararite, one of David's three foremost warriors, who held a lentil field against the Philistines.
key: Shammah son of Agee the Hararite was one of David's three chief mighty men (2 Samuel 23).
When Israel's troops fled from the Philistines, he took his stand in a field full of lentils (2 Samuel 23).
He defended the field and struck down the Philistines, and the LORD brought about a great victory (2 Samuel 23).

shammah_2540.name: Shammah
shammah_2540.who: Shammah of Harod, one of David's thirty mighty men.
key: Shammah of Harod is listed among David's thirty mighty men (2 Samuel 23).
Chronicles lists him as Shammoth of Harod among David's mighty men (1 Chronicles 11).

shaphat_2553.name: Shaphat
shaphat_2553.who: The father of the prophet Elisha, from Abel-meholah.
key: God told Elijah to anoint Elisha son of Shaphat of Abel-meholah as prophet after him (1 Kings 19).
Elisha left his oxen, kissed his father and mother goodbye, and followed Elijah (1 Kings 19).
Elisha is identified as Shaphat's son when the kings of Israel, Judah, and Edom seek him (2 Kings 3).
During Samaria's siege, the king of Israel swore to behead Elisha son of Shaphat (2 Kings 6).

sheba_2567.name: Sheba
sheba_2567.who: A son of Raamah and great-grandson of Ham, named in the table of nations after the flood.
key: Sheba is listed as a son of Raamah, son of Cush, in the table of nations (Genesis 10).
Chronicles repeats him with his brother Dedan among Raamah's sons (1 Chronicles 1).

sheba_2568.name: Sheba
sheba_2568.who: A son of Joktan in the line of Shem, named in the table of nations after the flood.
key: Sheba is listed among the thirteen sons of Joktan, a descendant of Shem through Eber (Genesis 10).
Chronicles repeats him among Joktan's sons (1 Chronicles 1).

shebna_2578.name: Shebna
shebna_2578.who: A steward over the royal household in Jerusalem whom Isaiah said God would remove and replace with Eliakim.
key: Shebna was the steward over the royal household in Jerusalem (Isaiah 22).
Isaiah rebuked him for carving out a grand tomb for himself (Isaiah 22).
The LORD declared he would hurl Shebna away and give his office to Eliakim son of Hilkiah (Isaiah 22).

shechem_2589.name: Shechem
shechem_2589.who: A descendant of Manasseh through Gilead and ancestor of the Shechemite clan.
key: Shechem son of Gilead headed the clan of the Shechemites in Manasseh's census (Numbers 26).
His clan received an inheritance among the tribe of Manasseh west of the Jordan (Joshua 17).

shelomith_2607.name: Shelomoth
shelomith_2607.who: A Gershonite Levite, son of Shimei, listed among family heads when David organized the Levites.
key: When David organized the Levites, Shelomoth was listed among the sons of Shimei (1 Chronicles 23).
He and his brothers Haziel and Haran were heads of fathers' houses of Ladan (1 Chronicles 23).

shemaiah_2637.name: Shemaiah
shemaiah_2637.who: A man hired by Nehemiah's enemies to frighten him into hiding in the temple.
key: Nehemiah visited Shemaiah son of Delaiah, who was confined to his home (Nehemiah 6).
Shemaiah urged Nehemiah to hide in the temple, claiming men were coming to kill him (Nehemiah 6).
Nehemiah refused, realizing Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him to make Nehemiah sin (Nehemiah 6).

shemaiah_2643.name: Shemaiah
shemaiah_2643.who: Shemaiah of Nehelam, a false prophet among the exiles in Babylon who opposed Jeremiah.
key: Shemaiah of Nehelam prophesied to the exiles in Babylon, though the LORD had not sent him (Jeremiah 29).
He wrote to the priest Zephaniah, urging him to put Jeremiah in the stocks (Jeremiah 29).
Zephaniah read the letter to Jeremiah (Jeremiah 29).
The LORD declared Shemaiah would have no descendant to see the good he would do for his people (Jeremiah 29).

shemeber_2648.name: Shemeber
shemeber_2648.who: The king of Zeboiim in Abraham's day, one of the kings of the valley who rebelled against Chedorlaomer.
key: Shemeber king of Zeboiim joined the kings of the valley in rebelling against Chedorlaomer (Genesis 14).
The four eastern kings defeated them in the Valley of Siddim and carried off Lot from Sodom (Genesis 14).

shemer_2649.name: Shemer
shemer_2649.who: The owner of the hill of Samaria, which King Omri bought to build Israel's new capital.
key: King Omri bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver (1 Kings 16).
Omri built a city on the hill and named it Samaria after Shemer (1 Kings 16).

shepho_2665.name: Shepho
shepho_2665.who: A son of Shobal and grandson of Seir the Horite, named among the early inhabitants of Edom.
key: Shepho is listed as a son of Shobal, son of Seir the Horite (Genesis 36).
Chronicles repeats him among Shobal's sons (1 Chronicles 1).

sheshai_2671.name: Sheshai
sheshai_2671.who: One of the three sons of Anak, a clan of giants living at Hebron when Israel entered Canaan.
key: The twelve spies saw Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai, descendants of Anak, at Hebron (Numbers 13).
Caleb drove the three sons of Anak out of Hebron (Joshua 15).
Judah defeated Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai at Hebron, formerly called Kiriath-arba (Judges 1).

shiphrah_2710.name: Shiphrah
shiphrah_2710.who: One of two Hebrew midwives in Egypt who feared God and refused Pharaoh's order to kill Israelite baby boys.
key: Pharaoh ordered Shiphrah and Puah, Hebrew midwives, to kill every Hebrew baby boy at birth (Exodus 1).
They feared God and let the boys live (Exodus 1).
Questioned by Pharaoh, they said Hebrew women gave birth before the midwives arrived (Exodus 1).
God dealt well with the midwives and gave them families (Exodus 1).

shitrai_2713.name: Shitrai
shitrai_2713.who: Shitrai of Sharon, the official in charge of King David's herds that grazed in Sharon.
key: Shitrai the Sharonite was over the herds that pastured in Sharon (1 Chronicles 27).
He was among the stewards who managed King David's property (1 Chronicles 27).

shobi_2722.name: Shobi
shobi_2722.who: An Ammonite from Rabbah, son of Nahash, who brought supplies to David during Absalom's revolt.
key: Shobi son of Nahash came from Rabbah of the Ammonites (2 Samuel 17).
When David fled from Absalom to Mahanaim, Shobi, Machir, and Barzillai brought beds, utensils, and food (2 Samuel 17).
They provided for David's people, who were hungry, weary, and thirsty in the wilderness (2 Samuel 17).

shua_2726.name: Shua
shua_2726.who: A daughter of Heber in the tribe of Asher, named in Chronicles' genealogy.
key: Shua was the daughter of Heber, a grandson of Asher (1 Chronicles 7).
She is named with her brothers Japhlet, Shomer, and Hotham (1 Chronicles 7).

simeon_2742.name: Simeon
simeon_2742.who: A righteous man in Jerusalem who held the infant Jesus in the temple and praised God for his salvation.
key: Simeon was a righteous, devout man in Jerusalem, waiting for the consolation of Israel (Luke 2).
The Holy Spirit had revealed he would not die before seeing the Lord's Christ (Luke 2).
Led by the Spirit into the temple, he took the infant Jesus in his arms and praised God (Luke 2).
He blessed Joseph and Mary and told Mary a sword would pierce her own soul (Luke 2).

simon_2746.name: Simon the Zealot
simon_2746.who: One of the twelve apostles, called the Zealot or the Cananaean to distinguish him from Simon Peter.
key: Matthew lists him among the twelve apostles as Simon the Cananaean (Matthew 10).
Mark also names him among the Twelve whom Jesus appointed (Mark 3).
Luke calls him Simon the Zealot in his list of the apostles (Luke 6).
After Jesus' ascension he was with the apostles praying in the upper room (Acts 1).

simon_2747.name: Simon
simon_2747.who: One of the brothers of Jesus, named by the people of Nazareth when they took offense at him.
key: The people of Nazareth named Simon among Jesus' brothers, with James, Joseph, and Judas (Matthew 13).
Knowing his family, they took offense at Jesus, who did few mighty works there (Mark 6).

simon_2748.name: Simon the leper
simon_2748.who: A man of Bethany, known as Simon the leper, at whose home Jesus was anointed shortly before his death.
key: Shortly before the Passover, Jesus was at the home of Simon the leper in Bethany (Matthew 26).
There a woman poured costly ointment on Jesus, who said she had prepared his body for burial (Mark 14).

simon_2749.name: Simon of Cyrene
simon_2749.who: A man from Cyrene whom Roman soldiers compelled to carry Jesus' cross to the crucifixion.
key: As Jesus was led out to be crucified, soldiers compelled Simon of Cyrene to carry his cross (Matthew 27).
Mark notes he was coming in from the country and was the father of Alexander and Rufus (Mark 15).
Luke says they laid the cross on him to carry behind Jesus (Luke 23).
